comparison: Perfect alignment on lysine-less control experiments (C34-C38, C67-C68). Both evaluations find this evidence SUPPORTED. Reviewer 1 explicitly commends the K-less vectors as essential controls, matching OpenEval's assessment that this definitively demonstrates direct target ubiquitylation.

Complete agreement on linker length effects (C52-C54, C73). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept linker optimization as essential controls, while OpenEval notes the mechanistic interpretation (C54) is somewhat speculative but reasonable.

Full concordance on lysine-rich reporter findings (C58-C62). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept these as extending the assay's utility without concerns, matching OpenEval's assessment of technical feasibility.

Strong agreement on FBXL12 findings (C46-C51, C76-C78). Both SUPPORTED. Reviewer 1 highlights FBXL12 as a strength. OpenEval adds caution that claim C78 ('every target tested') should be interpreted carefully given limited examples shown. Peer R5 includes C79 (prospective PROTAC utility) which OpenEval addresses separately in R12.

High concordance on RiPA validation against known PROTAC selectivity (C4, C31-C33, C69, C74, C83). Both SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers find data convincing and confirm assay utility. OpenEval emphasizes convergence with published PROTAC studies validates predictive capability. Peer R1 includes C5 (literature context) which OpenEval addresses in R16.

Partial alignment on system limitations (C80-C82). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED as reasonable assessments of scope/limitations. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting concerns about high-throughput feasibility and empirical PROTAC design challenges. Peer R9 includes C84 (prospective applications) which OpenEval addresses separately in R12 as UNCERTAIN.

Strong agreement on dose-dependent degradation and optimization parameters (C26-C29, C66). Both SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept these as methodological details supporting functionality. OpenEval emphasizes empirical demonstration of 10-fold E3 ligase excess requirement. Peer R2 does not include C25 or C65 which OpenEval groups with these claims.

Agreement on background context and field challenges (C3, C16-C18, C23, C63). Both SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept this framing as established knowledge motivating the study. OpenEval notes these accurately represent the field based on cited literature. Peer R10 includes additional background claims (C13-C15) that OpenEval addresses in R15.

Both address overarching conclusions about system functionality (C45, C64). OpenEval R10 is SUPPORTED, viewing these as summary statements validated by collective evidence. Peer R8 is SUPPORTED, with editor and reviewers affirming the technology's value and data quality. Peer R8 also includes C56 (kinetics) and C65 (dose-dependence) which OpenEval addresses in R7 and R1 respectively.

Agreement on mechanistic validation with inhibitors and additional targets (C42-C44). Both SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept broad applicability demonstration. OpenEval emphasizes convergence of experimental results with literature and mechanistic controls. Peer R4 includes C30 and C39 which OpenEval addresses in R2 and R9 respectively.

Overlap on kinetic measurement capability (C55-C56). OpenEval R7 is SUPPORTED for real-time measurements as significant technical advance. Peer R8 includes C56 among broader system capabilities, also SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 1 praising kinetics measurement in living cells.

Divergence on prospective applications (C79, C84). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN as forward-looking statements about PROTAC development utility not yet demonstrated. Peer R9 rates UNCERTAIN but focuses on different limitations (high-throughput feasibility, empirical design challenges). Both acknowledge uncertainty but emphasize different aspects.

Divergence on FBXL12 PROTAC utility (C79). OpenEval R12 rates UNCERTAIN as anticipatory claim about future applications. Peer R5 rates SUPPORTED, treating FBXL12 identification as a strength, though acknowledges practical PROTAC development remains to be demonstrated.

Both address Aurora kinase B findings (C39). OpenEval R9 is SUPPORTED, viewing this as extending differential E3 ligase selectivity to another family member. Peer R4 groups this with broader applicability findings (C30, C42-C44), also SUPPORTED.

Overlap on literature validation context (C5, C32-C33). OpenEval R16 is SUPPORTED, noting these accurately cite prior literature validating RiPA predictions. Peer R1 includes these among core validation findings, also SUPPORTED, emphasizing data quality and assay utility.

Overlap on background literature (C13-C15). OpenEval R15 is SUPPORTED for extensive background context (C6-C15, C19-C22, C24). Peer R10 includes subset (C13-C15) among motivating context, also SUPPORTED. Both treat as established knowledge.

OpenEval R11 addresses mechanistic speculation about ternary complex formation (C70-C72, C75) rated UNCERTAIN as inferred but not directly proven. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific mechanistic hypotheses.

OpenEval R17 addresses literature context for universal substrate reporters (C57) rated SUPPORTED based on Schapira et al. citation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing this contextual claim.
